s.autores.rawlinson.institucion: British East India Company; collaborator of the British Museum
s.autores.rawlinson.especialidad: British officer and diplomat who copied the trilingual Behistun inscription and was a central figure in the decipherment of cuneiform.
s.autores.rawlinson.aportaciones.0: Between 1835 and 1847 he copied the inscription of Darius I on the Behistun rock (Old Persian, Elamite and Babylonian), the "Rosetta Stone" of cuneiform.
s.autores.rawlinson.aportaciones.1: He published the translation of the Old Persian version (1846–1847) and made progress in reading the Babylonian version.
s.autores.rawlinson.aportaciones.2: He directed the edition The Cuneiform Inscriptions of Western Asia, which made thousands of texts from the British Museum available to researchers.
s.autores.rawlinson.aportaciones.3: He took part in the Royal Asiatic Society test of 1857, which showed that Akkadian could be read reliably.
s.autores.rawlinson.postura: His interest was above all historical and linguistic: he looked in the royal inscriptions for information on the Assyrian and Babylonian empires rather than for an interpretation of the myths.
s.autores.hincks.institucion: Anglican rector of Killyleagh (Church of Ireland); independent researcher
s.autores.hincks.especialidad: Irish clergyman and philologist, considered by many the true decipherer of the Akkadian writing system.
s.autores.hincks.aportaciones.0: He showed that Akkadian cuneiform signs represent syllables and not single letters, and that the same sign can have several readings (polyphony).
s.autores.hincks.aportaciones.1: He identified the use of determinatives and ideograms within syllabic writing.
s.autores.hincks.aportaciones.2: He sensed that cuneiform writing had not been invented by speakers of a Semitic language, an idea that paved the way for the recognition of Sumerian.
s.autores.hincks.aportaciones.3: He was one of the four participants in the Royal Asiatic Society test of 1857.
s.autores.hincks.postura: He worked as a linguist: his goal was to establish the values of the signs methodically, a precondition for any serious reading of the myths.
s.autores.oppert.especialidad: Franco-German orientalist, one of the founders of Assyriology and an early advocate of the existence of Sumerian.
s.autores.oppert.aportaciones.0: He took part in the French scientific expedition to Mesopotamia (1851–1854) and published its results.
s.autores.oppert.aportaciones.1: He was one of the four translators in the Royal Asiatic Society test of 1857.
s.autores.oppert.aportaciones.2: He proposed the name "Sumerian" for the non-Semitic language underlying cuneiform writing and defended its existence against those who denied it.
s.autores.oppert.aportaciones.3: He promoted the teaching of Assyriology in France from the Collège de France.
s.autores.oppert.postura: He held that behind Babylonian culture there was an earlier people with a different language, the Sumerians, which changed the way the origin of the Mesopotamian myths was understood.
s.autores.george-smith.especialidad: Self-taught engraver who became an Assyriologist at the British Museum; he identified the Babylonian flood story.
s.autores.george-smith.aportaciones.0: In 1872 he identified on a tablet from Ashurbanipal's library (Tablet XI of the Epic of Gilgamesh) a flood story very similar to that of Genesis, and presented it on December 3, 1872, before the Society of Biblical Archaeology.
s.autores.george-smith.aportaciones.1: He traveled to Nineveh sponsored by the Daily Telegraph (1873) and found new fragments of the epic.
s.autores.george-smith.aportaciones.2: He published the first overall reconstruction of the Babylonian creation and flood stories.
s.autores.george-smith.aportaciones.3: He died in Aleppo in 1876 during his third expedition.
s.autores.george-smith.postura: He read the texts in comparison with the Bible, as was usual in his time; his discovery showed that the flood story had Mesopotamian antecedents.
s.autores.layard.institucion: Excavations sponsored by the British Museum; later a diplomat and politician
s.autores.layard.especialidad: Pioneering archaeologist who excavated Nimrud and Nineveh and brought the great Assyrian reliefs and winged bulls to the British Museum.
s.autores.layard.aportaciones.0: He excavated Nimrud (ancient Kalhu) from 1845 and brought to light Assyrian palaces with reliefs and lamassu.
s.autores.layard.aportaciones.1: At Kuyunjik (Nineveh) he discovered the palace of Sennacherib and the first rooms with tablets from the so-called library of Ashurbanipal.
s.autores.layard.aportaciones.2: His very popular books awakened interest in Assyria in Europe.
s.autores.layard.postura: An excavator rather than a philologist; his methods were those of his time, focused on recovering spectacular pieces.
s.autores.rassam.especialidad: Assyrian Christian archaeologist born in Mosul, Layard's collaborator and discoverer of most of Ashurbanipal's library.
s.autores.rassam.aportaciones.0: In 1853 he discovered at Nineveh the North Palace of Ashurbanipal, with thousands of tablets, among them those of the Epic of Gilgamesh.
s.autores.rassam.aportaciones.1: He found the bronze gates of Balawat (1878).
s.autores.rassam.aportaciones.2: He discovered the Cyrus Cylinder in Babylon (1879).
s.autores.rassam.postura: His work was in the field; for a long time his role was overshadowed by that of British colleagues.
s.autores.kramer.pais: United States (born in the Russian Empire)
s.autores.kramer.especialidad: Sumerologist who reconstructed and popularized Sumerian literature from thousands of fragments from Nippur.
s.autores.kramer.aportaciones.0: He identified, joined and translated fragments of tablets from Nippur scattered between Philadelphia and Istanbul, recovering myths such as the Descent of Inanna or Enki and Ninhursag.
s.autores.kramer.aportaciones.1: He offered the first synthesis of Sumerian mythology (1944).
s.autores.kramer.aportaciones.2: He popularized Sumerian culture with History Begins at Sumer, where he listed numerous "firsts" of civilization.
s.autores.kramer.aportaciones.3: He collaborated with Jean Bottéro on a large anthology of Mesopotamian myths.
s.autores.kramer.postura: He saw the Sumerian myths as the oldest known expression of religious and cosmological ideas, and read them in their literary and cultural context, not as literal chronicles.
s.autores.jacobsen.institucion: Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago; Harvard University
s.autores.jacobsen.especialidad: Sumerologist and historian of Mesopotamian religion.
s.autores.jacobsen.aportaciones.0: He published the standard study of the Sumerian King List (1939).
s.autores.jacobsen.aportaciones.1: He proposed the model of "primitive democracy" in the assemblies of the Sumerian cities.
s.autores.jacobsen.aportaciones.2: He traced a history of Mesopotamian religion by stages in The Treasures of Darkness.
s.autores.jacobsen.aportaciones.3: He translated a broad selection of Sumerian poetry (The Harps that Once…).
s.autores.jacobsen.postura: He interpreted the gods as expressions of the "numinous" perceived in natural and social phenomena, with a religion that evolved from gods of nature to ruling and personal gods.
s.autores.landsberger.institucion: University of Leipzig; University of Ankara; Oriental Institute of Chicago
s.autores.landsberger.especialidad: Assyriologist and lexicographer, teacher of several generations of specialists.
s.autores.landsberger.aportaciones.0: He founded the series Materialien zum sumerischen Lexikon (MSL), an edition of the Mesopotamian lexical lists.
s.autores.landsberger.aportaciones.1: He advocated studying Babylonian culture "on its own conceptual terms" (Eigenbegrifflichkeit).
s.autores.landsberger.aportaciones.2: After being expelled from Leipzig by the Nazi regime, he taught in Ankara and then in Chicago, where he contributed to the Chicago Assyrian Dictionary.
s.autores.landsberger.postura: He insisted on not projecting modern categories onto the texts: the Babylonians had to be understood through their own categories.
s.autores.lambert.especialidad: Standard editor of Babylonian religious and wisdom literature.
s.autores.lambert.aportaciones.0: He edited Babylonian wisdom literature in a work that is still fundamental (1960).
s.autores.lambert.aportaciones.1: With Alan Millard he published the edition of Atrahasis (1969), the Babylonian story of the creation of man and the flood.
s.autores.lambert.aportaciones.2: His posthumous edition of the Babylonian creation myths (2013) includes the Enuma Elish.
s.autores.lambert.aportaciones.3: He criticized the idea that Genesis depends directly on the Babylonian myths, pointing out differences as well as parallels.
s.autores.lambert.postura: A rigorous philologist, he distrusted grand theories; he stressed that the Enuma Elish is a relatively late composition in the service of Marduk and Babylon.
s.autores.millard.especialidad: Assyriologist and Semitist specializing in the relations between Mesopotamia and the biblical world.
s.autores.millard.aportaciones.0: He coedited the Atrahasis epic with W. G. Lambert (1969).
s.autores.millard.aportaciones.1: He studied the Assyrian eponyms (limmu), the basis of the chronology of the Neo-Assyrian Empire.
s.autores.millard.aportaciones.2: He has written on literacy and writing in the ancient Near East.
s.autores.millard.postura: He compares the Mesopotamian texts with the Bible from a conservative position, highlighting both parallels and fundamental differences.
s.autores.bottero.especialidad: Assyriologist and historian of Mesopotamian religion and thought, a great popularizer in French.
s.autores.bottero.aportaciones.0: With S. N. Kramer he collected and commented on the main Sumerian and Akkadian myths in Lorsque les dieux faisaient l'homme (1989).
s.autores.bottero.aportaciones.1: He translated the Epic of Gilgamesh into French (1992).
s.autores.bottero.aportaciones.2: He studied Mesopotamian divination as a form of rational and systematic thought.
s.autores.bottero.aportaciones.3: He popularized aspects of daily life, such as Mesopotamian cuisine based on recipes on tablets.
s.autores.bottero.postura: He understood the myths as "calculated imagination": reasoned answers, in narrative form, to questions about the origin of the world and of human beings.
s.autores.oppenheim.institucion: Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago
s.autores.oppenheim.especialidad: Assyriologist, editor of the Chicago Assyrian Dictionary and author of an influential overview of Mesopotamia.
s.autores.oppenheim.aportaciones.0: He was editor in charge of the Chicago Assyrian Dictionary during its decisive phase.
s.autores.oppenheim.aportaciones.1: He studied dreams and their interpretation in the ancient Near East.
s.autores.oppenheim.aportaciones.2: He wrote Ancient Mesopotamia: Portrait of a Dead Civilization, a classic synthesis of the discipline.
s.autores.oppenheim.postura: He argued, in a famous section, that a coherent "Mesopotamian religion" could not be written: the myths reach us filtered through scribes and elites and do not necessarily reflect lived religion.
s.autores.reiner.institucion: Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago
s.autores.reiner.especialidad: Assyriologist specializing in Babylonian magic, omens and astrology; editor of the Chicago Assyrian Dictionary.
s.autores.reiner.aportaciones.0: She directed the Chicago Assyrian Dictionary for more than two decades (1973–1996).
s.autores.reiner.aportaciones.1: She edited the incantation series Šurpu (1958).
s.autores.reiner.aportaciones.2: With David Pingree she edited the Babylonian planetary omens (Enuma Anu Enlil).
s.autores.reiner.aportaciones.3: She studied the relationship between stars, magic and medicine in Astral Magic in Babylonia.
s.autores.reiner.postura: She read Babylonian astrology and magic as internally coherent systems of knowledge, without anachronisms.
s.autores.civil.institucion: Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago
s.autores.civil.especialidad: Catalan Sumerologist, one of the greatest specialists in the Sumerian language and lexical lists.
s.autores.civil.aportaciones.0: For decades he edited the series Materialien zum sumerischen Lexikon (MSL).
s.autores.civil.aportaciones.1: He edited and studied "The Farmer's Instructions", a Sumerian agricultural manual.
s.autores.civil.aportaciones.2: He translated the Hymn to Ninkasi, with its famous beer recipe (1964).
s.autores.civil.aportaciones.3: He contributed to the Chicago Assyrian Dictionary and to the grammar of Sumerian.
s.autores.civil.postura: He insisted on the philological basis: the interpretation of a myth depends on understanding its vocabulary and grammar precisely.
s.autores.jeremy-black.especialidad: Sumerologist, driving force behind the Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature (ETCSL).
s.autores.jeremy-black.aportaciones.0: He created and directed the ETCSL at Oxford, which put online, free of charge, some 400 Sumerian literary texts with English translation.
s.autores.jeremy-black.aportaciones.1: With Anthony Green he wrote the illustrated dictionary of Mesopotamian gods, demons and symbols (1992).
s.autores.jeremy-black.aportaciones.2: He studied Sumerian poetics with the methods of literary theory.
s.autores.jeremy-black.postura: He read the Sumerian myths as literature, paying attention to poetic form, metaphors and the audience they were addressed to.
s.autores.anthony-green.especialidad: Archaeologist and historian of Mesopotamian art, specializing in religious iconography.
s.autores.anthony-green.aportaciones.0: Coauthor with Jeremy Black of the illustrated dictionary Gods, Demons and Symbols of Ancient Mesopotamia (1992), the basic reference on the iconography of gods, demons and symbols.
s.autores.anthony-green.aportaciones.1: He has studied the iconography of protective and demonic figures in Mesopotamian art.
s.autores.anthony-green.postura: He relates image and text: many symbols (such as the winged disk or the genies with bucket and cone) can only be understood by comparing them with the ritual texts.
s.autores.wiggermann.especialidad: Assyriologist specializing in Mesopotamian protective spirits, demons and hybrid beings.
s.autores.wiggermann.aportaciones.0: He edited the Babylonian rituals of protective figurines and related them to the images of genies in art (1986/1992).
s.autores.wiggermann.aportaciones.1: He identified in them the apkallu, primordial sages, as ritual figures of protection, not as visitors from the sky.
s.autores.wiggermann.aportaciones.2: He wrote standard studies on hybrid beings (Mischwesen) and on Nergal and the Underworld.
s.autores.wiggermann.postura: He interprets demons and hybrid figures within the Mesopotamian religious and ritual system, as agents of protection or punishment in the service of the gods.
